messages:
Jen (Support): FYI ACME is hitting a 401 on our /v1/generate endpoint and they say there is no request id in the response headers. Customer sent a redacted curl but it strips headers. What exact repro bits should I ask for to escalate?
Sam (SRE): Ask for the raw curl with headers (use -i or -v) or the full HTTP transaction. We need the X-Redwood-Request-Id header (or absence), timestamp, and their client IP/region. Also ask for proxy/nginx logs if they sit behind a gateway.
Jen (Support): Got it. Any quick curl examples I can paste to them?
Diego (SDK): Paste this minimal repro snippet — it shows headers and body and prints the request id:
```bash
# show response headers + body, then grep our header
curl -i -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' | awk 'BEGIN{h=1} /\r$/{h=0} {print} /X-Redwood-Request-Id:/ {print "--FOUND--"}'
# or verbose to capture headers sent by upstream/proxy
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' 2>&1 | grep -i "request-id"
```
Sam (SRE): If they use our SDKs, ask for the SDK debug token (client-side) or call to get last request id. If they can run the SDK debug collector, that bundles logs + headers.
Morgan (Platform): In the Console UI you can go to Logs -> API Requests, set the time range and search by customer org id. The Request details pane shows the header as X-Redwood-Request-Id and the routed model/version. Screenshot of that pane is super helpful.
Diego (SDK): Mobile snippets to grab last request id:
```swift
// iOS (objc/swift wrapper)
let id = RedwoodSDK.shared.lastRequestId()
print("last request id: \(id)")
```
```java
// Android
String id = Redwood.getInstance(context).getLastRequestId();
Log.i("rw", "last request id=" + id);
```
Look for log lines like: "response status=401 request_id=abc123" in their app logs.
Jen (Support): If they say "no header at all" could a proxy strip it?
Sam (SRE): Yes. Common culprits: reverse-proxies, API gateways, or browser CORS preflight hiding headers. Ask them to check upstream/proxy access logs for any X-Redwood-Request-Id or X-Request-Id fields. For nginx check `access.log` entries or look for `proxy_set_header` behavior.
Morgan (Platform): Also request:
- exact timestamp (UTC) of the failure
- region used (us-east-1 / eu-west-1)
- the full response body and raw headers (not just our SDK error message)
- whether they saw retries or redirects
If they can reproduce, ask for a HAR file from Chrome DevTools: Network -> right click -> Save all as HAR with content.
Diego (SDK): Example HAR/DevTools guidance to send to customer:
1) Open DevTools -> Network tab
2) Reproduce the request
3) Right-click -> Save all as HAR with content
Attach that file here (redact prompt text if needed).
Jen (Support): What about redaction? They are worried about PII in prompts.
Sam (SRE): Tell them to either replace the prompt with "<REDACTED_PROMPT>" in the captured payload or send us a minimal repro that demonstrates auth failing (same headers but safe body). We only need the headers, status, and correlation tokens.
tracebot: Created ticket INC-2026-3482 and attached customer initial message.
Diego (SDK): Also add this quick grep for upstream logs (example nginx):
```bash
# find X-Redwood-Request-Id in nginx access logs
grep -i "X-Redwood-Request-Id" /var/log/nginx/access.log || grep -i "request_id" /var/log/nginx/access.log
# or show proxied header value via curl to your gateway
curl -I -s https://your-gateway.example/endpoint -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" | grep -i "X-Redwood-Request-Id"
```
Sam (SRE): If they provide a request id (e.g. abc123) include that and the exact timestamp and region in the escalation. Our infra can look it up across edge/ingest and find the routed backend.
Jen (Support): Perfect. I'll send the curl + -i example, ask for HAR or SDK debug token, and request upstream logs + timestamp. Tagging @Sam (SRE) in case they reply with the trace id. Thanks :thumbsup:
Sam (SRE): Happy to take it once they send the raw headers / request id.
Jen (Support): I'll update the ticket when they reply.
